qa_rejections_7d.notes: Low-resolution, purple-tinted ISS TV feed with a dark, near-empty opening frame and a repeated shot at 32 to 34 s; nothing visibly goes wrong. Interchangeable with today's sharper HD spacewalk (02).
Every shot is the same white cloud mass from orbit, with no visible turn and no landfall footage; hurricane content is in the review's do-less list and the hazards lane is the weakest.

Clean high-speed liftoff but no danger, no turn, and the capsule is cropped out of most frames; it is interchangeable with the many launch Shorts already queued (shuttle, Artemis, Columbia) and 08 tells a stronger launch story.

Calm training dive with no danger on screen; about six seconds of blurry water-on-glass close-ups in the middle and a static hatch shot. The Squalus history is a good idea but the footage cannot carry it.

Single static test-stand camera for 40 seconds with six seconds of no fire in the middle; no danger or human hook, and 'every valve fired on command' and 'nobody touching it but the computer' are not in the source.

Hoist-cam footage is smeared with heavy color noise and the top-down frames are hard to read in the first second; a third Kodiak Jayhawk hoist in this batch, interchangeable with recent Alaska hoists.
Artemis II liftoff again (already 14-03, 14-32, 16-08 in the queue or posted), and about ten seconds in the middle show a tiny rocket sitting on the pad before ignition.
Calm routine hoist: the hoist cam hangs over a small patch of deck for most of the Short, mostly in a narrow fit strip, and the 964-foot ship is never shown at scale.
The release does not say how the night ended, so the outcome line is unsupported; one locked shot for 25 seconds and the fifth lava fountain Short in the queue.
Calm rehearsal with a static group photo near the end and no real danger; repeats the recent spacecraft uprighting test and splashdown Shorts. Dropped.
Calm routine landing on a helideck where the patient walks aboard; the helideck shots repeat and nothing on screen is at risk. Dropped.
Builds cleanly now, but it is calm routine training: no danger on screen, and 9 to 14s is name patches and a tail fin. Dropped.

Strong fireball opening, but the crop turns the trainer car into a black slab, the clip is a low-stakes demo with a crowd in the stands, and the source never shows the fire put out, so the last line ends on a cliffhanger. Dropped.

Clean build and accurate facts, but the footage is a calm test ride: long stretches of a cable over grass and a stationary basket interior, with no danger or human hook on screen. Too close to today's run of NASA Shorts (Starliner, Soyuz, Crew-9, DART, Orion). Dropped.

Only one launch in the source; lines 2 and 3 play over people standing beside the sled and a man signaling, and the sled in flight is a tiny dot. Routine test with no danger, and a second USS Gerald R. Ford Short in the same batch as -06. Dropped.
